module

public import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fin.Rotate

@[expose] public section

variable {n : ℕ}

theorem lt_finRotate_of_ne_last {i : Fin (n + 1)} (hi : i ≠ Fin.last n) :
    i < finRotate _ i := by
  rw [Fin.lt_def, coe_finRotate_of_ne_last hi, Nat.lt_add_one_iff]

sources_consulted: /opt/formal-conjectures/.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Fin/Basic.lean, especially finAddFlip and its application lemmas
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration, lt_finRotate_of_ne_last; this file introduces no definitions and cites no external mathematical source. Its hypothesis is exactly i.val < n, so finRotate (n + 1) sends i to the strictly larger index with value i.val + 1 without wraparound. Mathlib's lt_finRotate_iff_ne_last independently confirms the implication. At n = 0 the domain is Fin 1 and the hypothesis is correctly impossible; the excluded last index rotates to zero. The only explicit caller is the polygon-angle lemma in Geometry/2d.lean, which assumes at least three vertices and handles both wraparound cases before applying this helper. No direct problem-file uses were found. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiled successfully, proving the modular-successor formula and relevant characterizations, evaluating rotations of sizes 0–6, and checking singleton, nonvacuous, and wraparound cases. The reviewed theorem has no sorryAx dependency. No repository files were edited.
